Repo: /opt/nxeon-v2, branch design/v2 (a design fork called "Nexion" of the Nxeon hosting platform). Read /opt/nxeon-v2/CLAUDE.md first for the operating rules of this tree. This session just built a light/dark theme system for the account dashboard (light is new; dark is the original/default look, unchanged). You are ONE of 4 parallel background agents fixing different, non-overlapping parts of this light-mode pass. COORDINATION RULE: do not run ./rebuild.sh or restart the nxeon-v2-web service except for your own verification (fine if you need one cycle to see your fix land), and do not create git commits — the orchestrating session will do one final rebuild+commit across all 4 agents' work.

YOUR TASK: the user screenshotted /dashboard/services ("My Services") in light mode and said the "Manage" buttons on that page were a flat, ugly, low-contrast mid-slate-blue, and more generally "the buttons on the my services page are terrible." Nobody has investigated or fixed this page yet.

FILES: the page shell is app/dashboard/services/page.tsx (a hero header — mostly already using theme-safe tokens like `text-white`/`text-tx-dim`, but double check it actually reads correctly in light mode) which renders components/customer/services/ServicesView.tsx (the real content: a service-type filter, a table of services with a "Manage" button + "..." menu per row, and likely some summary/quick-action cards) and components/customer/services/FreeServicesClaim.tsx (shown only for accounts without a free-tier service yet).

WHAT TO DO:
1. First, actually SEE the bug: log in as the sandbox customer (credentials at /root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt, or see the login flow in scripts/shot.mjs) and screenshot /dashboard/services in both light and dark mode — set `localStorage.setItem('nx-theme','light')` + `document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme','light')` (or remove the attribute for dark) before/after navigating, same trick used elsewhere in this session. Compare the two.
2. Find every element rendering with a hardcoded/literal color that doesn't adapt to the theme, rather than a theme CSS custom property from app/globals.css (`--color-*` tokens). This exact bug pattern has already been found and fixed repeatedly elsewhere in this codebase this session — recognizable shapes include: a `bg-white` (bare, not `bg-white/NN`) utility used to mean "always literally white," which broke because `--color-white` now means "ink" in light mode (fix: swap to a literal `bg-[#fff]` if the surface is meant to always be a saturated/dark badge regardless of theme, or restyle properly for both themes if it's meant to be a real page-level button); an `Icon` component rendered with no `tone` prop inside a colored badge, which then paints itself in the icon's own hardcoded default tone instead of inheriting the badge's intended text color (fix: pass `tone="inherit"` to the Icon); a card with a hand-written literal dark rgba gradient background (e.g. `bg-[linear-gradient(...,rgba(10,22,48,...),...)]`) that doesn't get any lighter in light mode; `text-white/NN` (opacity-modified) used inside something that ISN'T actually a light-mode-adapted surface. The established, consistent fix vocabulary in this codebase is: use existing `--color-*` tokens (see app/globals.css) wherever the surface should genuinely change between themes; use the `.nx-dark-island` CSS class (also in app/globals.css, and used on e.g. components/nx/SupportView.tsx's hero, components/nx/MatrixPanel.tsx's hero) on any element that is a fixed, always-dark decorative surface with its own art/gradient that was never meant to lighten; use literal colors (`text-[#fff]`, `bg-[#fff]`) ONLY for things sitting on a genuinely fixed saturated surface that must stay the same regardless of theme (e.g. a colored button/badge), never for things that sit on the actual page background.
3. Fix the "Manage" button specifically, and anything else on this page (filter chips, table row styling, any small cards/icons) that reads badly in light mode. The goal is for this page to look as considered/finished in light mode as pages like /dashboard/support or the VPS server panel already do (both already fixed this session — feel free to look at how components/nx/SupportView.tsx or components/customer/vpspanel/v2/kit.tsx (`Panel`, `card card-glass`) do things, as a reference for the visual language you should be matching, without necessarily copying their exact markup).

CONSTRAINTS: only touch files under app/dashboard/services/ and components/customer/services/, plus app/globals.css if you need a genuinely new, clearly-scoped CSS rule (comment why, matching the style of comments already in that file). Do NOT touch components/nx/ServicesAurora.tsx (the page's animated backdrop canvas) — that's being fixed by a parallel agent as part of a sitewide sweep of similar backdrop components; leave it exactly as it is. Do not touch components/customer/vpspanel/v2/*, components/nx/DeployView.tsx, or components/nx/RewardsView.tsx — those are owned by other parallel agents.

Verify with `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit`. Write a final summary of every change and a before/after description of what was wrong.

The 5 code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but 6 `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. 7 8 Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the 9 direction and the history of what has been built. 10 11 --- 12 13 ## Where you are, and what that changes 14 15 This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is 16 meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: 17 18 ```bash 19 hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. 20 ``` 21 22 **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: 23 24 ```bash 25 npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build 26 ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. 27 ``` 28 29 **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also 30 runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, 31 terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A 32 `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, 33 then: 34 35 ```bash 36 scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 37 ``` 38 39 It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) 40 and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. 41 42 **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on 43 node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not 44 deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's 45 commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. 46 47 ## The tree 48 49 | | | 50 |---|---| 51 | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | 52 | Branch | `design/v2` | 53 | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | 54 | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | 55 | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | 56 | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | 57 | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | 58 59 `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and 60 it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` 61 builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. 62 63 Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node 64 and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing 65 to the other. 66 67 ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here 68 69 node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because 70 three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept 71 attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the 72 production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox 73 seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. 74 75 Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two 76 levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong: 77 78 ```bash 79 scripts/node1.sh cards "dashboard" # find concept cards by title 80 scripts/node1.sh board # list that card's attachments 81 scripts/node1.sh pull # copy them to /tmp/board/ 82 scripts/node1.sh db "select …" # read-only query against PROD 83 scripts/node1.sh sh '' # anything else 84 ``` 85 86 **That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production 87 database and the mail server. If you genuinely need to change something on node-1, 91 **stop and ask the owner first.** 92 93 ## Rules that are not negotiable 94 95 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs 96 or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real 97 upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had 98 hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not 99 reintroduce that shape.
